findings.reason: The protected source is the canonical sorted two-pointer greedy solution: cookies are scanned from smallest to largest and each adequate cookie satisfies the least greedy remaining child. It is compact, conventional, clearly named, and expert interview quality, so no inert candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies public LeetCode problem 455 and its runnable Python contract, including a nonempty greed list and possibly empty cookie list. The O(g log g + s log s) time and O(g + s) space claims correctly include both Python sorts, the linear scan, and sorting workspace.

The immutable native source is bound to verified submission 2064928300. Its in-place sorts, child pointer, ascending cookie scan, adequacy comparison, one-step advancement, and returned match count are identical to the protected app-local algorithm and data flow; only annotations and the LeetCode class wrapper differ.

The 31-, 127-, and 511-item reverse-ordered tiers span more than 16x and force full sorting and matching. The current source passed all 7 opaque correctness executions and all three performance tiers at 1.01x the reference runtime. A correct control that repeatedly searches and removes the smallest adequate cookie passed every output but failed only the runtime verdict at 206.35x.

The Approach exactly matches the protected target: it proves the smallest-adequate-cookie exchange, justifies discarding undersized cookies, states the sort and scan costs, and accounts for Python sorting memory. Its symmetric greedy alternative and one-to-one, empty-list, duplicate, and equality boundaries are all accurate.

The hash-bound modular Reference was checked directly against the live public statement. It preserves the parent-and-children model, at-most-one-cookie rule, both exact source examples with their full count reasoning, all three constraints, and the post-constraints note equating the task with problem 2410. The unsupported legacy third example was removed.
